nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_001
nodes.question: What strategies can successfully reduce total social costs in transitioning to a climate-neutral economy?
nodes.answer: Using avoid, shift, or improve strategies can successfully reduce total social costs, with the strongest effects seen in packages that address all three dimensions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_002
nodes.question: How does one of the OECD reports suggest addressing the trade-off between human well-being and environmental concerns?
nodes.answer: One of the OECD reports suggests adopting a well-being lens in climate change mitigation policies to place humans at the centre of climate action, aiming to separate the improvement in human well-being from the consumption of natural resources and greenhouse gas emissions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_003
nodes.question: What are some internal efforts that individual states undertake to protect against climate risk?
nodes.answer: Individual states undertake efforts such as implementing environmental taxes, applying the polluter pays principle, and providing subsidies for green transformation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_004
nodes.question: What is the focus of the IPCC Working Group III in their contribution to the Sixth Assessment Report on Climate Change?
nodes.answer: The IPCC Working Group III focuses on the mitigation of climate change and strategies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in their contribution to the Sixth Assessment Report.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What are the two political strategies that countries implement to address transboundary pollution problems?
nodes.answer: The two political strategies are mitigation and adaptation.
nodes.paragraph: Most countries facing a transboundary pollution problem implement one of two political strategies: mitigation and adaptation. Mitigation policies aimed at reducing carbon emissions instead adaptation measures meant to reduce pollution damage, considering the dramatic effects of the accumulation and increase in the concen- tration of pollutant which persists in the atmosphere for decades. While mitigation consists of any means aimed at curtailing the pollution emission of countries, adap- tation is increasingly considered a policy response to climate change alongside the Stability of International Environmental Agreements: Effects mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, its measures consist of a set of actions that prevent or decrease the adverse effects of accumulated pollution. The literature look - ing at IEAs combining mitigation and adaptation measures is quite recent. Benchek - roun et al. (2017), Borrero and Rubio (2022), Breton and Sbragia (2019), Lazkano et al. (2016), Masoudi and Zaccour (2017), Rohrer and Rubio (2024) and Masoudi and Zaccour (2018) focus on the strategic role of mitigation and adaptation in the IEAs as a tool to combat climate change.

nodes.question: How do institutional pressures influence climate mitigation and adaptation strategies, according to Daddy et al. (2020)?
nodes.answer: Daddy et al. (2020) highlight the impact institutional pressures have on climate mitigation and adaptation strategies. They found that these pressures can significantly influence the decisions and actions taken by organizations in addressing climate change challenges.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_009
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which two sectors contribute to nearly half of all strategies in the climate action plans reviewed?
nodes.answer: Energy and mobility contribute to nearly half, at 43%, of all strategies.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Cities are increasingly creating climate action plans (CAPs), but it is unclear what poten - tial these have for cities to sufficiently address the climate crisis. We conducted a review of 157 CAPs published by U.S. cities between 2018 and early 2023 to assess the current state of the practice. Through a qualitative content analysis of these plans, we analyzed explicit planned strategies to describe what sectors receive the most attention, what types of actions cities commonly take, and what domains of urban life are most leveraged to solving climate change. We found that a strong plurality (40%) of all strategies target municipal operations, nearly half (49%) of all strategies are focused on creating new plans and assessments, and energy and mobility contribute to nearly half (43%) of all strategies. These findings identify shortcomings of conventional climate action planning, including opportunity to work across sectors, to create stronger interventions, and to integrate cli - mate action across all urban domains, including food and water. Climate action planning has become a ubiquitous practice for cities, and cities climate action will continue to in - crease in importance over the next decade.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_010
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What have past research findings indicated about the emphasis of climate action strategies in American cities?
nodes.answer: Past research has indicated a disproportionate emphasis on mitigation strategies, while adaptation is growing in importance.
nodes.paragraph: While past research has documented a disproportionate emphasis on mitigation strategies in American cities (Ozcan and Strauss 2021 ), adaptation is growing in importance (Tang et al. 2010 ; Shi et al. 2015 ; Grafakos et al. 2019 ), though research has shown that many cit - ies struggle to integrate mitigation and adaptation into their CAPs (Aboagye and Sharifi 2024 ). Adaptation can occur at state and national levels; however, adaptation is inherently a local issue, where climate change renders cities vulnerable to impacts such as flooding and drought, among other challenges (Corfee-Morlot et al. 2010 ; Bierbaum et al. 2012 ; Hughes 2015 ; Greve 2016 ). Adaptation strategies may also appear in other planning documents, including resilience plans, which have increased in popularity in recent years (Lambrou and Loukaitou-Sideris 2021 ). 1.2 Local powers and local climate policy We noted above U.S. cities tendencies to target mitigation strategies on emissions from municipal facilities and other domains that are easily managed by their jurisdictional pow - ers. For this research, we study a dataset of CAPs published over a recent five-year period, asking in part whether this trend has changed or if municipal operations still dominate cli - mate action planning in the U.S.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Climate change mitigation efforts_qna_012
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What key strategies are being implemented in Spain to address climate change according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Spain is implementing the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law, the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) 2021-2030, the National Plan for Adapting to Climate Change (PNACC), and the Just Transition Strategy.
nodes.paragraph: Notable among such actions is the EuropeanClimate Law, enacted in June 2021, which sets a legally binding target of net zero GHG emissions by 2050 and requires both Member States and EU institutions to take the necessary measures to meet this target. This Law also sets an intermediatetarget for 2030 of reducing GHG emissions in the EU as a whole by 55% (from 1990 levels). The success of these agreements critically hinges on the implementation of effective policies at the national level. In this paper, we focus on a particular countrywithin the EU, namely, Spain, in which the basic pillars of such a strategy are the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law, the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) 2021 2030, the National Plan for Adapting to Climate Change (PNACC by its Spanish abbreviation) and the Just Transition Strategy; see Banco de Espa a (2021 ). For example, within the framework of the Law on Climate Change and Energy Transition, proposals have been made for notable changes to patterns of mobility and the creation of low-emission zones in major cities.
